quizName: DMV Practice Test #15 25 Questions • Passing Score 19

questions.question: When turning, you should:

options.text: Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
Turn your head and shoulders together.
Turn your shoulders, but not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: When turning, look ahead to where you want to go. Move only your head, keep your shoulders still, and keep your eyes level.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped on the side of the road with flashing lights. You should:

options.text: Stop on the roadway behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait until the emergency vehicle moves.
Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, change lanes to give it more space. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: A motorcycle needs _____ stopping distance compared to a car.

options.text: about the same
more
less

questions.correctAnswerText: about the same
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need about the same distance to stop as cars do.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Ride on the shoulder of the road.
Follow other vehicles more closely.
Stay farther behind other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind other vehicles.
questions.explanation: At night, increase the distance between you and other vehicles. Slow down and adjust your lane position as needed.

questions.question: If parked cars are on your right and there is no oncoming traffic, you should ride:

options.text: on the left side of your lane
on the right side of your lane
in the middle of your lane

questions.correctAnswerText: on the left side of your lane
questions.explanation: Ride on the left side of your lane to avoid car doors opening and people stepping out between vehicles. If there is oncoming traffic, stay in the middle of your lane for safety.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, ride in:

options.text: the left side of the lane
the middle of the lane
the right side of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: the middle of the lane
questions.explanation: Stay in the middle of your lane when being passed. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle is dangerous. Riding on the far side may make the driver cut back too soon.

questions.question: While riding, you should wear:

options.text: hearing protection to prevent damage from engine and wind noise
a helmet to protect your hearing
a baseball cap

questions.correctAnswerText: hearing protection to prevent damage from engine and wind noise
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing over time, even with a helmet. Use hearing protection when riding.

questions.question: When riding with other motorcyclists in a staggered formation:

options.text: use it all the time
don't use it when entering or leaving a highway
use it when going through curves

questions.correctAnswerText: don't use it when entering or leaving a highway
questions.explanation: Staggered formation is usually good, but switch to single-file when going through curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: Making eye contact with another driver:

options.text: means they see you
doesn't guarantee they will yield to you
guarantees they will yield to you

questions.correctAnswerText: doesn't guarantee they will yield to you
questions.explanation: Don't assume eye contact means a driver will yield. Drivers often look at motorcyclists and still don't see them.

questions.question: The main difference between goggles and a windshield is:

options.text: Goggles protect your eyes from wind, but a windshield doesn't
A windshield protects your eyes from wind, but goggles don't
A windshield prevents eyes from watering better than goggles

questions.correctAnswerText: Goggles protect your eyes from wind, but a windshield doesn't
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes from wind, but most windshields do not. A windshield is not a good replacement for goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
You may go through the intersection carefully.
You must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red traffic light. You must stop and wait for a green arrow or green light before turning in that direction.

questions.question: A sudden shaking of the front wheel and handlebars is usually caused by:

options.text: Wrong tire pressure or uneven weight distribution.
The front wheel not being fastened tightly to the frame.
Hitting something with the front tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wrong tire pressure or uneven weight distribution.
questions.explanation: This shaking usually comes from incorrect tire pressure, improper weight distribution, or unsuitable accessories.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: The light is about to turn red.
The light is about to turn green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light is about to turn red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns that the signal will change to red soon. Slow down and stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection, continue through it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slippery when wet
Lanes shift
Yield

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns you that the road ahead may be slippery when wet.

questions.question: In general, which position in a lane is best to ride in?

options.text: The left position
The right position
There is no single best position.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no single best position.
questions.explanation: No single position is always best. A smart rider changes position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: To turn safely on a motorcycle, you should always:

options.text: Lean toward the direction of the turn.
Slow down during the turn.
Turn using only the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean toward the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: Always lean in the direction you are turning. Slow down before you enter the turn, not during it.

questions.question: When riding behind a car in the center of the lane:

options.text: The driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
The driver will have trouble seeing you.
You should avoid this position.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Riding in the center of the lane behind a car lets the driver see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirrors more often than side mirrors, so this position is safer.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while braking, you should:

options.text: Release the front brake right away, then apply it again.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Keep the front wheel locked until you stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away, then apply it again.
questions.explanation: If the front wheel locks while braking, release the brake immediately and then apply it again.

questions.question: When preparing to pass a vehicle on the left, which part of your lane should you ride in?

options.text: The left portion
The center portion
The right portion

questions.correctAnswerText: The left portion
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when preparing to pass. This gives you a better view ahead and signals to other drivers that you plan to move into the next lane.

questions.question: Where should you position your motorcycle when entering a curve?

options.text: The outside of the curve
The inside of the curve
Wherever traffic and road conditions require

questions.correctAnswerText: Wherever traffic and road conditions require
questions.explanation: Every curve is different. Choose a lane position that fits the current conditions and adjust as needed.

questions.question: When making a normal stop on a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
Use only the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: For a normal stop, use both the front and rear brakes together and downshift.

questions.question: If you wear a riding jacket in hot weather, you should:

options.text: Take frequent breaks to cool down.
Remove it to stay cool in the sun.
Keep it on for protection and to reduce dehydration.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it on for protection and to reduce dehydration.
questions.explanation: A riding jacket protects you during a crash, no matter the weather. In hot weather, it also prevents dehydration. Many jackets are designed to keep riders from overheating.

questions.question: Is it a good idea to use all three lane positions?

options.text: No, because you cannot get used to any part of the lane.
No, because it confuses other drivers.
Yes, when road and traffic conditions change.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, when road and traffic conditions change.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Move your position as conditions require.

questions.question: How high can handlebars be positioned?

options.text: No higher than shoulder height.
No higher than waist height.
As high as or higher than shoulder height.

questions.correctAnswerText: No higher than shoulder height.
questions.explanation: Handlebars cannot be at or above shoulder height. It is illegal to operate a motorcycle with handlebars that high.

questions.question: Which surface is least likely to cause poor traction for a motorcycle?

options.text: Dry pavement.
Dirt or gravel road.
Shiny surface.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement.
questions.explanation: Many surfaces are hazardous for motorcycles. Wet pavement, loose gravel or sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lines, and metal covers are more dangerous than dry pavement.
